description: TifawtTech is a Moroccan team of developers and AI enthusiasts who love turning ideas into practical solutions. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we’re tackling the challenge “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data,” using AI and Earth observation data to support sustainable agriculture. With skills in Python, machine learning, data science, backend, APIs, and React, we’re driven by curiosity and innovation.
summary:
TifawtTech is a farmer-centred agricultural decision-support platform designed to help smallholder farmers make more informed farming decisions in the face of climate uncertainty and water scarcity.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the platform combines NASA POWER climate data with farm-level information to help farmers explore crop choices, plan agricultural zones, and understand water-related constraints.

Farmers can map their land, organize it into management zones, identify water sources, plan irrigation channels, explore crop suggestions, and investigate crop rotation options. The platform also provides climate and weather insights to support more informed agricultural planning.

Designed with Moroccan farming conditions in mind, TifawtTech focuses on making environmental information more accessible through an interactive, multilingual experience.

Our goal is to connect Earth observation data with practical farm planning and encourage more climate-aware and sustainable agricultural decisions.
details:
TifawtTech – Project Details

1. The Problem

Smallholder farmers face increasing challenges caused by climate variability, water scarcity, and limited access to accessible agricultural information. Choosing suitable crops, organizing farm areas, managing water resources, and planning crop rotations can be difficult, especially when farmers lack access to digital agricultural decision-support tools.

These challenges are particularly relevant in Morocco, where many agricultural regions experience semi-arid conditions and increasing pressure on water resources.

2. Our Solution

TifawtTech is a farmer-centred agricultural decision-support platform that combines NASA climate information, interactive farm mapping, and practical planning tools.

Instead of presenting complex environmental data through technical dashboards alone, the platform transforms available information into a guided farm-planning experience.

3. Main Features

A. NASA-Based Climate Insights

TifawtTech integrates NASA POWER historical meteorological data to provide climate context, including temperature and precipitation information. These indicators help farmers better understand environmental conditions when planning agricultural activities.

B. Interactive Farm Mapping

Farmers can select their land, define farm boundaries, and divide their fields into management zones using an interactive map. Each zone can be planned and managed independently.

C. Crop Suggestions

The platform provides preliminary crop suggestions based on available climate information and farmer-provided preferences. These suggestions are intended to support exploration rather than replace validated agronomic recommendations.

D. Crop Rotation Exploration

TifawtTech includes a crop rotation exploration and advice prototype to encourage farmers to consider alternative planting choices and more sustainable agricultural practices.

E. Water Resource Planning

Farmers can identify water sources, place them on their farm map, and draw irrigation channels. The platform also provides water-related planning context to help organize agricultural zones.

F. Farm Monitoring and Progress

Farmers can explicitly record planting, watering, and soil-care activities. The platform connects farm progress to actual recorded actions instead of automatically assuming that suggested crops have been planted.

G. Multilingual and Farmer-Friendly Experience

The interface supports English, French, and Arabic, including right-to-left Arabic navigation. Its guided workflow, visual interactions, and gamified progress features aim to make agricultural planning more accessible.

4. NASA Data and Technology

NASA POWER is the currently integrated NASA data source, providing historical climate information relevant to farm planning.

The application also uses Open-Meteo for forecast and modelled weather information, clearly distinguished from NASA observations.

The technology stack includes:

  • Next.js 15 and React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • GSAP and Motion for interface animations
  • JavaScript-based interactive mapping and browser storage
  • NASA POWER API
  • Open-Meteo weather services
  • OpenStreetMap mapping resources

5. Innovation and Added Value

TifawtTech brings together climate context, interactive farm mapping, management zones, water planning, crop suggestions, and crop rotation exploration in one farmer-oriented experience.

Its key innovation is the connection between Earth observation information and practical agricultural planning. Rather than requiring farmers to interpret complex datasets independently, it provides a guided interface that helps them explore their land and consider different farming decisions.

The platform is designed with Moroccan agricultural realities in mind, particularly the needs of smallholder farmers operating under water and climate constraints.

6. Intended Impact

TifawtTech aims to:

  • Improve access to climate-related agricultural information.
  • Encourage more informed crop selection and rotation planning.
  • Support better organization of farm zones and water resources.
  • Promote climate-aware and sustainable farming practices.
  • Make digital agricultural tools more accessible to Moroccan farmers.

7. Limitations and Future Development

TifawtTech is currently a prototype and decision-support tool. Crop recommendations and rotation guidance require further agronomic validation. Water-source distances are approximate and do not represent hydraulic flow simulations. The platform does not claim validated yield prediction, groundwater detection, or measured zone-level soil conditions.

Future development will focus on strengthening the crop rotation decision engine, improving scientific data integration, validating recommendations with local agricultural experts, and expanding real-world farmer testing.

The platform is intended to support farmers and agricultural experts, not replace professional agronomic advice or field measurements.
